questions.question: For a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$ with strategies $s_i\colon\Theta_i\to A_i$, which condition defines a Bayesian Nash equilibrium $s^*$?
options: Each player's realised type best responds to the other players' realised actions
Each player maximises her payoff for the realised type profile $\theta$
The profile maximises the sum of all players' ex ante expected payoffs
Each type with $p(\theta_i)>0$ best responds to $s^*_{-i}$ given her beliefs

questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$ with strategies $s_i\colon\Theta_i\to A_i$, suppose every type set $\Theta_i$ is a singleton. What is a Bayesian Nash equilibrium of this game?
options: A profile that maximises each player's worst-case payoff
A Nash equilibrium of the underlying complete-information game
A dominant-strategy equilibrium of the underlying game
Any profile, since without uncertainty every profile is optimal

questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$ with strategies $s_i\colon\Theta_i\to A_i$, action $a_i'$ is strictly dominant for type $\theta_i'$, which has positive probability. What does this imply for Bayesian Nash equilibria?
options: Type $\theta_i'$ plays $a_i'$ only if the other players play dominant actions
Every type of player $i$ plays $a_i'$ in every Bayesian Nash equilibrium
Type $\theta_i'$ plays $a_i'$ in every Bayesian Nash equilibrium
Type $\theta_i'$ may mix between $a_i'$ and other actions

questions.question: Two players each decide whether to pay toward a shared good worth 1 to both; it exists if at least one pays. Paying costs $\tfrac{1}{4}$ or $2$, each with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, independently, and only the payer knows her cost. Player 2 pays exactly when her cost is $\tfrac{1}{4}$. What should player 1 do when her cost is $\tfrac{1}{4}$?
options: Pay: $\tfrac{3}{4}$ beats the $\tfrac{1}{2}$ expected from not paying
Not pay, since free-riding on player 2 is worth $1$ for sure
Pay, since not paying would leave her with nothing
Not pay, as paying nets only $\tfrac{1}{4}$, below $\tfrac{1}{2}$

questions.question: In a Bayesian game, player 1 of type $a$ believes player 2's type is $x$ with probability $0.8$ (the marginal $p(x)$ is $0.6$). Player 2 plays $L$ if $x$ and $R$ if $y$. Player 1's $U$ pays 1 against $L$ and 4 against $R$; $D$ pays 2 against either. What is type $a$'s best response?
options: $U$, since it yields $2.2$
$D$, since $U$ yields only $1.6$
$U$, since against $R$ it yields $4$
$D$, since $U$ yields only $1$

questions.question: Players 1 and 2 have independent private costs, $\tfrac{1}{4}$ or $2$ with equal chance, of contributing to a public good worth 1 to each, which is provided if at least one contributes. In the Bayesian Nash equilibrium each contributes exactly when her cost is low. How likely is the good to be provided?

Player 1 chooses Enter or Out; simultaneously player 2, Tough (probability $0.3$) or Weak, chooses Fight or Accommodate. If player 1 enters she gets 2 against Accommodate and $-1$ against Fight; Out gives 0. Whatever player 1 does, Tough strictly prefers Fight and Weak strictly prefers Accommodate. Which profile is the Bayesian Nash equilibrium?
options: Out; Tough fights, Weak accommodates
Enter; both types of player 2 accommodate
Enter; Tough fights, Weak accommodates
Out; both types fight

questions.question: For a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$ with strategies $s_i\colon\Theta_i\to A_i$ in which every type has positive probability, why is the type-by-type (interim) best-response condition equivalent to maximising the ex ante expected payoff $\sum_\theta p(\theta)v_i(s(\theta);\theta)$ over strategies $s_i$?
options: Because the ex ante payoff ignores the prior and weights every type of player $i$ equally
Because each type's action enters only its own term, which has positive weight
Because every type's interim payoff coincides with the ex ante payoff
Because only the most likely type of player $i$ affects the ex ante payoff

questions.question: Two players decide simultaneously whether to contribute ($C$) or decline ($D$) to a good worth 1 to each that exists if anyone contributes. Each knows only her own cost of contributing: $\tfrac{1}{4}$ with probability $0.9$, otherwise $2$, independently. Which strategy profile is a Bayesian Nash equilibrium?
options: Each player contributes exactly when her own cost is $\tfrac{1}{4}$
Only player 1's cost-$\tfrac{1}{4}$ type contributes
Nobody contributes, whatever the realised costs are
Every type of each player contributes, whatever her cost

questions.question: In the usual interim payoff calculation for a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$ with strategies $s_i\colon\Theta_i\to A_i$, which information specifies the distribution of the other players' actions conditional on a player's own type?
options: Their strategies (what each of their types would do) and the prior $p$
Their realised types, so that she can predict their actions exactly
Their realised actions, which she observes before making her own choice
Nothing about their behaviour; she only needs her own payoffs

questions.question: In a contribution game (good worth 1 to each, provided if someone contributes; private costs $\tfrac{1}{4}$ or $2$, equally likely and independent), the opponent contributes ($C$) exactly when her cost is $\tfrac{1}{4}$. A player whose cost is $2$ compares $C$ with declining ($D$). Which conclusion is correct?
options: $C$, since the good is worth more with two contributors
$C$: its $-1$ beats the $-\tfrac{1}{2}$ expected from declining
$D$, which yields nothing, against $-\tfrac{1}{2}$ from $C$
$D$, worth $\tfrac{1}{2}$ in expectation, against $-1$ from $C$

questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$ with strategies $s_i\colon\Theta_i\to A_i$, player 1 does not observe player 2's type, and the high-cost type has positive conditional probability. Player 2 changes only what her unrealised high-cost type would do, keeping her other type's action. Why can this change player 1's best response?
options: Because player 1 observes player 2's type before choosing
Because unrealised types change the prior $p$
Because player 1's own type set depends on player 2's strategy
Because player 1 averages over all of player 2's types

questions.question: Every finite Bayesian game has at least one Bayesian Nash equilibrium. Which statement about this existence result is correct?
options: A pure-strategy BNE always exists, since private types remove the need to mix
Existence requires each type to have a strictly dominant action
It may require mixed strategies, by Nash's theorem for the ex ante game
Existence follows only when types are independent across players

questions.question: A public good worth 1 to each of two players is provided if at least one of them contributes ($C$) rather than declines ($D$). Contributing costs her privately known type: $0.4$ with probability $q$, else $2$, independently. For which $q$ is the profile in which both players contribute iff their cost is $0.4$ a Bayesian Nash equilibrium?

Each of two players privately learns whether her cost of contributing is $\tfrac{1}{4}$ or $2$ (probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$ each, independent). A good worth 1 to both appears if at least one contributes ($C$); declining is $D$. Is the profile in which every type contributes a Bayesian Nash equilibrium?
options: Yes, since the good is then provided with probability one
Yes, since realised types contribute in every play of the game
No, although only the cost-$2$ types would gain by deviating
No: every type gains by declining against a sure contributor

questions.question: Using the positive-probability-type equilibrium convention for a finite Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$ with strategies $s_i\colon\Theta_i\to A_i$, type $\theta_i'$ has prior probability $p(\theta_i')=0$, and action $a_i'$ is strictly dominant for it. Must $s_i^*(\theta_i')=a_i'$ hold in every Bayesian Nash equilibrium?
options: Yes, since strictly dominant actions are always played
No: only types with positive probability are constrained
Yes, since every type in $\Theta_i$ must best respond
No, since zero-probability types must play a mixed action

questions.question: In a contribution game (good worth 1 to each if anyone contributes; private costs $\tfrac{1}{4}$ or $2$, each with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$), the BNE has each player contribute ($C$) iff her cost is $\tfrac{1}{4}$, else decline ($D$). Both turn out to have cost $\tfrac{1}{4}$ and then learn this. Which statement is correct?
options: Each now prefers $D$, though $C$ was optimal given her beliefs
The profile was not a BNE, since an ex post deviation pays
Each would still prefer $C$, since BNE actions are ex post optimal
Learning types changes nothing, since the two cost values are equally likely.

questions.question: Contributing ($C$, rather than declining, $D$) to a good worth 1 to each of two players (provided if anyone contributes) costs a privately known $\tfrac{1}{4}$ with probability $0.9$, else $2$, independently. In a symmetric BNE, cost-$2$ types decline and cost-$\tfrac{1}{4}$ types contribute with probability $r$. What is $r$?

Types have prior $p(a,x)=0.4$, $p(a,y)=0.1$, $p(b,x)=0.2$, $p(b,y)=0.3$. Player 2 plays $L$ if $x$, $R$ if $y$. Player 1's $U$ pays 3 against $L$ and 0 against $R$; $D$ pays 1 against $L$ and 2 against $R$. Which strategy (action of type $a$, action of type $b$) best responds?
